name: Nerthus

attributes.attribute: cult shaped the rituals of Celtic goddesses
worshipped on a sacred island no one could enter

sources: Tacitus. The Agricola and the Germania. Translated by H. Mattingly. New York: Penguin Books, 1948. Pp. 134-135.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nerthus is a Germanic goddess. Some features of her cult shaped the rituals of Celtic goddesses. Tacitus described her worship on a sacred island. No one could enter the island. Celtic tradition often used such islands to picture the Otherworld. At times Nerthus left her island to travel among her followers. Her followers drew her forth in a wagon pulled by oxen and greeted her with celebration. All warfare stopped while the goddess was abroad. The land was held to grow fruitful wherever she passed. Once the circuit closed, she went back to her holy island. Her escort was then killed, since none who had seen the goddess might keep his life. The image of a goddess on a cart appears in Celtic contexts too. The Celts may also have practiced sacrifice of living persons.

okr.objective: Nerthus is a Germanic goddess whose cult reached the Celtic world.
